bank.title: Across Subjects · Demo
bank.description: Explore mathematics, science, and humanities with 12 sample questions. Then bring your own question banks for any subject.
bank.author: quitsar

questions.prompt: Describe the shaded shape in this geometry diagram.

images.alt: A blue shaded ring between two concentric circles with an unshaded center

acceptedAnswer.display: An annulus: the region between two concentric circles.
acceptedAnswer.feedback: Mention the inner and outer circular boundaries.

questions.explanation: An annulus is bounded by two circles with the same center and different radii.

options.rationale: Annular describes a ring-shaped arrangement.
Linear describes an arrangement along a line.
Reticular describes a net-like pattern.

questions.explanation: Annular means ring-shaped; an annulus is the region between two concentric circles.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe visible features of the shaded ring in the demo geometry diagram?

options.rationale: The shaded region surrounds an unshaded circular center.
The inner and outer edges are circles.
A diagram of a shape does not specify its material.
The shape alone does not establish a purpose.

questions.explanation: The diagram shows a ring with circular boundaries. It provides no information about physical material or purpose.

questions.prompt: Which geometric pattern does the shaded region form?

images.alt: A blue shaded ring between two concentric circles with an unshaded center

options.rationale: The visible rim forms a ring.
There is no line-shaped distribution.
The diagram does not form a network.

questions.explanation: The shaded region forms a ring between two concentric circles.

questions.prompt: Write the relationship between distance, constant speed, and time.
questions.explanation: At constant speed, each unit of time adds the same distance. Multiplying speed by elapsed time gives distance.

questions.prompt: A cyclist travels at a constant 14 km/h for 0.3 hours. How far do they travel?

options.rationale: This is ten times smaller than the product.
This is ten times larger than the product.

questions.prompt: Which statements correctly describe the simplified cell diagram conventions used in this demo?

options.text: The outer boundary represents the cell membrane.
options.rationale: The outer boundary is used as the membrane symbol.

options.text: The large central oval represents a nucleus.
options.rationale: The oval is labeled as the nucleus in the demo.

options.text: Every component is drawn to accurate biological scale.
options.rationale: It is a schematic and is not to scale.

options.text: The diagram shows every organelle present in a living cell.
options.rationale: A simplified schematic omits many structures.

questions.explanation: Schematic conventions support learning but cannot substitute for actual microscopy. For this two-correct-option item: one correct alone earns 0.5 partial; one correct and one incorrect earns 0.

questions.prompt: Select all structures explicitly labeled in this simplified diagram.

images.alt: Simplified oval cell with an outer boundary labeled membrane and a central oval labeled nucleus

options.rationale: The outer boundary is explicitly labeled.
The central oval is explicitly labeled.
No ribosome is shown or labeled.
No Golgi apparatus is shown or labeled.

questions.explanation: Identify only what is explicitly depicted. This question demonstrates multiple-select image recognition.

questions.prompt: Which event is shown earliest on this sample timeline?

images.alt: Timeline ordered left to right: printing press in Europe around 1450, first crewed Moon landing in 1969, and World Wide Web proposal in 1989

options.rationale: Around 1450 precedes both 1969 and 1989.
1969 comes after around 1450.
1989 is the latest date on this timeline.

questions.explanation: Read the dates to compare chronological order. Around 1450 is the earliest date shown.

questions.prompt: What is a primary source in historical research?

acceptedAnswer.display: Evidence created during the period being studied or by someone directly involved in the events.
acceptedAnswer.feedback: Give an example, such as a diary entry or an original letter.

questions.explanation: A primary source provides direct evidence about a historical question. Whether a source is primary depends on the research question.

questions.prompt: For a study of daily life in 1910, which is a primary source?

options.rationale: It records firsthand observations from the period.
It interprets earlier evidence and is a secondary source for this question.
It offers a later interpretation of the period.

questions.explanation: A diary from the period can provide firsthand evidence of daily life. Its perspective and reliability still need evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which questions help evaluate a historical source?

options.rationale: Authorship and timing help establish the source’s context.
Audience and purpose may influence what a source includes.
Old sources can contain errors or biased accounts.

options.text: Must it agree with my view to be useful?
options.rationale: A source can challenge your interpretation and still be valuable evidence.

questions.explanation: Consider authorship, date, audience, purpose, and supporting evidence. Neither age nor agreement with your own view guarantees reliability.
